basis: Desmin-related skeletal myopathy; cardiomyopathy, conduction block and heart failure occur in 30-79%. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness, not intrinsic pulmonary disease.
Malignant perivascular/pericytic neoplasm; no specific additional organ site is established. Historical hemangiopericytoma terminology overlaps with solitary fibrous tumors.
Disorder of circadian sleep-wake regulation; no additional directly damaged organ is established.

Inherited lysine metabolism disorder; developmental delay reported in 2/2 annotated patients supports neurologic involvement, although clinical expression is variable and many individuals are asymptomatic.
Defining incisor anomaly; nasal stenosis 9/14 and choanal atresia 8/14; impaired GH response 5/7; holoprosencephaly 30-79% and learning disability 5/14 support the other axes.
Apolipoprotein amyloid deposition; renal medullary abnormalities and elevated creatinine in 80-99%. Cardiac amyloid is only 1-4%; other cardiac findings do not establish direct deposition.
Inherited recurrent patellar dislocation directly affects knee joint stability.
Localized dermal elastic tissue disorder producing persistent fibrous papules.
Neoplasm originating in the duodenum; neuroendocrine histology alone does not establish a separate endocrine disorder.
Familial intestinal enteropathy with villous edema and defining IgG2 immunodeficiency.
Broad chromosome 18 anomaly umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment predominates among clinical syndromes. Other organ defects vary substantially by rearrangement.
Spastic paraplegia and microcephaly define neurologic disease; optic atrophy defines ocular involvement. Sex reversal alone does not establish endocrine dysfunction.
Nerve sheath neoplasm arising in and occupying the heart; both cardiac site and peripheral nerve origin are defining.
Acquired impairment of learned motor actions from disruption of cortical motor-planning connections.
Microcephaly and developmental impairment define disease; scoliosis occurs in 4/7. Cerebral visual impairment is neurologic; recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
Defining intellectual disability, callosal agenesis and cerebellar abnormalities; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Hirsutism and facial features do not establish skin damage.
Tumor of hormone-producing gonadal granulosa cells, classified as an endocrine gland neoplasm.
Congenital bilateral absence of toes is a defining skeletal malformation.
Inherited palmoplantar epidermal hyperkeratosis; additional organ disease is confined to particular syndromic subtypes.
Cowden disease has defining skin and oral mucosal hamartomas. Thyroid, renal and breast carcinomas are separately diagnosed predisposition outcomes; isolated thyroid nodules do not prove dysfunction.
Spigelian hernia reflects an abdominal wall fascial defect. Cryptorchidism is reproductive; endocrine dysfunction or intrinsic bowel damage is not established.
Defining limb and brain malformations; neurogenic bladder and hydronephrosis in 1/1 annotated patient support renal involvement. Urinary infections and osteomyelitis are separate diagnoses.
Inherited lysine metabolism disorder. Neurologic impairment is occasional (5-29%); urinary amino acid abnormalities do not establish kidney damage.
Unspecified tubulin gene/protein entry without a defined disease or organ phenotype. No clinically defensible organ assignment can be inferred from the gene name alone.
Enteric duplication; rib defects, cord malformations and tricuspid abnormalities each annotated 80-99%. Respiratory distress is compressive without established intrinsic lung damage; cap reached.
